column1: # KNOWN SOFT EDGE, stated rather than smoothed over. The split between a node that SETS the style
# and one that INHERITS it is computed from instance override lists, and it does not fully close:
# 80 nodes classify as inherited, but two components named as their origin — `Warning` (7963:79675,
# Icons page) and `App menu` (6235:65668) — carry the style on no descendant of their own, and two
# more (`Tags` 18415:5427, `[S] Button X` 236:2205) do not resolve to a page at all. So `follows`
# is the honest reading of most of that bucket and a guess for some of it. It affects the order of
# work, never the total: 203 is measured directly and twice.
# 22 nodes rebound. 203 -> 141, measured by two sweeps that agree (and a cold sweep in between
# returned 92, which is the same under-report this file warns about — it is not the answer).
# 22 edits cleared 62 nodes, because 40 of them were instances that inherit. Tables, Controls
# and Analytics and charts are now completely clear; System messages is down to 1.
# Every one preserves today\'s appearance exactly. That was the bar: a rebind that changes how
# light mode looks is a design decision, not a rebind.
# ── THE REST OF THE FIX BUCKET IS NOT TOKEN WORK ──────────────────────────────
# Three nodes are WHITE ARTWORK ON A WHITE SURFACE — invisible as drawn. A token cannot be
# chosen for them without knowing the intent, and "preserving appearance" would preserve a bug.

column3: Header @32488:24634 — a white `Folder organiser` app icon in the Configr top bar. The
Configr header variant\'s own fill is a plain unbound #FFFFFF, so the icon is invisible.
The likely answer is `Navigation/Configr nav` (#656565 light, #FFFFFF dark): white is
right in dark and wrong in light, which is exactly what a static white cannot express.
Applying it CHANGES light mode from invisible to grey, so it needs a designer.
